behavior: Objects::prepareModel creates an opaque prepared LooseObjectSceneBinding for an identified single-body model. It records its actual private ObjectAnimation, placement, renderer owner, source hash, body/target record, registered flags and reference-root identity. Source identity permits independently scaled physical properties; it is not full shape/mass equality.

The link retains no renderer, animation or reference. Weak observer pointers can acquire a strong animation lease. Validation checks a distinct weak renderer owner, exact animation/placement and native pose identity, current renderer model and link registrations. A published link must match the current base placement; prepared links cannot lease a live animation.

Renderer map entry allocation happens during preparation. Publication inserts a prepared node and marks the link published. Cancellation, rollback, ordinary removal, prepared removal, cell removal and renderer destruction retire the registration. Retained shared handles, local checkpoints or animation leases cannot resurrect it.

WorldModel loose admission passes this exact prepared link to PhysicsSystem and PhysicsTaskScheduler. Physics retains a weak handle and a sticky linked flag, validates source/target identity during preparation, requires the exact model to be published before physical commit without consuming rejected preparation, and rejects retired/replaced/expired links. A deliberate renderer-free body still returns a null link; a formerly linked body never falls back to that mode.

World::synchronizeLooseWeaponPoses obtains the link directly from physics, without resolving World RenderingManager animation ownership. It validates each linked model before capturing/publishing root poses and retains its animation lease through the pass. The existing root-only/inverse-bind algorithm remains; this is an ownership guard, not per-node scene integration.
test_scope: Real owned-NIF native World factory, private MWRender::Objects and real Bullet loose body; exact live model lease persists after successful plan destruction and rejects changed source/record/flags/reference-root identities and renamed live physical node.

Four retirement contexts: ordinary removeObject, prepared model removal, removeCell, Objects destruction. Explicitly retain a shared link, animation lease and local checkpoint, restore old placement, and show no resurrection. After dropping the last link, weak expiry still rejects. World synchronization rejects while preserving reference position and physical pose/linear/angular velocities.

Detached physical admission invalidates after both never-published model cancellation and published-model rollback, with an animation lease retained in the latter. Wrong native source rejects while the link is otherwise valid. Physical admission never reaches the world, original transaction remains valid.

Linked physical commit rejects a still-prepared model without consuming the physics proposal or touching the world, then retries successfully after that model is published. Model rollback retires the now-published physical link.

A new valid model for the same reference has its own link/animation. The original physical owner rejects its retired link rather than following the replacement. Existing renderer-free admission test explicitly checks null link behavior.
